rejected.note: The rule's own title, “Computing and Extending Time; Time for Motion Papers”. It names the subjects of the subsections below and states none of them: no period, no condition, no party and no consequence. Every rule it names is quoted by an entry citing the subsection that states it.

The Office of Law Revision Counsel's amendment history -- the dates on which the Supreme Court prescribed each amendment and the dates each took effect. It is printed inside the <courtRule> element and is an editorial note about the rule rather than a passage of it. Which text is in force is the manifest's `asOf` and `contentHash`, which is where this map records it; an entry quoting the credit would be citing the Code's apparatus as though the Court had prescribed it.

A caption and nothing else: the element prints “Extending Time.” and opens paragraphs that carry the whole of what it is about. Unlike Rule 6(a), Rule 12(a) and Rule 12(b), which print a chapeau that states an applicability or an obligation their paragraphs then qualify, this one prints no sentence, so there is no passage here to decline and none to quote.
